sections.description: The opening question asks whether customers should be viewed as assets or costs ahead of any deeper discussion.
sections.title: Intro: asset vs cost center

sections.description: Notes that mature markets may see a shift from large clients toward smaller customers and invites consideration of their lifetime value.
sections.title: Market maturity and shift to smaller clients

sections.description: Questions whether to begin relationships as investments in assets that grow versus transactional approaches, and how this attitude permeates outreach and long-term impact.
sections.title: Investing in relationships for long-term value

summary: In this concise talk excerpt, Jeanne Bliss invites viewers to reframe customers as assets whose lifetime value should guide organizational choices. She contrasts investing in long-term relationships with treating customers as purely transactional, and notes that maturity in the market may shift attention toward smaller clients. The questioning voice highlights how the chosen mindset about customers potentially shapes outreach, support, and long-term business impact.
title: Asset vs Cost Center: Customer Lifetime Value Mindset
topics: Lifetime value as a strategic metric
